The hags, whose jaws are reduced to cartilage and whose gills function as mouth, are probably the oldest living fish family.
Many hags live in caves on coral reefs or along rocky shores.
The hags are usually seen swimming at low speeds near the bottom and their appearance is reminiscent of a viper or snake.
The toothy, flat hags (Myxicidae) often are mistaken for skates or sharks, but they actually have neither teeth nor true fins, but only fins that are actually their tails.
As with sharks and sharks' relatives like the sturgeon, hagfish and hag are living fossils.
